title: Artists who squandered royalties and the lack of a New Orleans business infrastructure
summary: Matassa recalls an artist given a $65,000 check who refused advice to buy a double house, and laments that many ended poor or bitter.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Yeah. Yeah. You know, one of the things that we talked about it because, you know, we'd go eat lunch and have breakfast together. And this is when he was trying to convert me to a born-again Christian too.
Smith's putting in the latter part.

Yeah. And we'd talk about some of the incidents that happened, you know. For instance, some artists who would say, oh, I never was paid unless… And we'd talk about the incidents where guys would come in and not fold their check before they go spend it, you know, and that kind of thing. And I can remember we had one guy. I was at his office when he cut him, not his first, but his first really big royalty check. At that time, it was probably in the 60s, 60, $65,000. And…

Let's skip that for now. If I feel like saying it later, I will. But it's only a couple of three that would fit that dollar and cents category. Right. 65,000. Right. Wow. And Joe and I tried to talk him into… See, already we let out the women. It can only be a male in this mystery. But tried to talk him into going to buy a double house. And the thought was that knowing that this particular artist was somebody who may never have another hit record and may never handle his personal finances correctly.
He's probably a person who didn't.

Didn't. Didn't. Hadn't up until then. There was no reason to believe they would do it anymore. Didn't do it. And say, look, why don't you buy a double house? We'll go with… You don't have to pay us. We'll help you find a place, neighborhood you like, house you like. And you can live in half of it. And you can get some money from the other half. Right. And your life will be better.

And of course, that… Forget it, right? Right. And the reason I'm saying it in this kind of allegorical sense almost is because there were other cases. The numbers weren't as big. And the talk wasn't that specific. But over and over, that kind of thing happened. And it's… Looking back on my life and how I saw what happened to other people, it's the saddest part of it all that maybe a dozen people out there who either are living… Now, as almost paupers or who died as paupers could have had nice lives.

Lived comfortably, lived well, and been a lot happier. Been a lot happier. Because, you know, I think you're probably aware of, and I certainly am, of some people who lived the ends of their lives or who are living the ends of their lives bitter.
Yeah. Saying… Yeah. I was ripped off.
I was stolen. Yeah. And some of them were, of course. You know. Some were. But… But…
A lot of times they did get royalty money.

And they didn't know how to deal with it. They didn't know how to deal with it. To spend it. And incidentally, I'd like to say this because this is really important. I think the effort that several people in this city have made over the last six, eight, ten years to try to develop a real business infrastructure in this city is because most of you have seen that other side of it and hope that legitimate managers and legitimate lawyers and legitimate whatever's, agents and so forth, would at least open the possibility that this wouldn't be so pandemic that everybody almost is suffering from this in one way or another. And for the most part, that hasn't happened. And so that's a job yet to be accomplished.
What? You don't think that exists today in this?

Not enough. Not enough. There are too many people who are still… are kind of wandering in the wilderness, you know, instead of in a real structured situation. And there are a few people who are very good at going out there and taking advantage of them. We've got a couple running around this city right now that we'd be a lot better off without. And it just, you know, it's kind of sad that it still hasn't happened. That's another story.
